title: Two Heads Are Better Than One: Generalized Cross-Domain Federated Learning via Dual-Prototype

problem.claim: Cross-domain federated learning seeks to train a generalized model across clients with heterogeneous domain distributions without sharing data.

gap.claim: Existing prototype-based methods have limited ability to balance generalized and domain-specific feature learning.

contributions.claim: FedOrthrus decomposes prototypes into generalized and domain-specific components to capture cross-client domain-invariant features and domain-specific features.
FedOrthrus aggregates generalized prototypes on the cloud server and uses clustering to adaptively construct domain-specific prototypes.
FedOrthrus uses distribution-aware prototype construction to dynamically assign the size of prototype components according to domain heterogeneity.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a novel dual-prototype guided federated learning framework named FedOrthrus.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three datasets report up to 14.56% accuracy improvement over traditional prototype-based federated learning methods.
Experiments on three datasets report up to 3.96% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art prototype-based federated learning methods.
The authors report that code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain federated learning trains generalized models across heterogeneous client domains without sharing data.
Existing methods use aggregated or clustered prototypes to align representations and share knowledge.
These methods struggle to balance generalized and domain-specific feature learning.
FedOrthrus introduces dual prototypes, combining aggregated generalized prototypes with clustered domain-specific prototypes and distribution-aware sizing.
Experiments on three datasets report accuracy improvements over traditional and state-of-the-art prototype-based methods.
